newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SARFU PAY 57 MILLION RANDS TO PREVENT DEFECTIONS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SARFU PAY 57 MILLION RANDS TO PREVENT DEFECTIONS.

text.p: South African authorities paid 57 million rand (12.5 million) to leading players to prevent a wholesale defection to the abortive World Rugby Corporation (WRC).

South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) president Louis Luyt told the union's annual meeting on Friday SARFU had paid 24 million rand to tie 27 of its 1995 World Cup winning squad to three-year contracts and allocated another 33 million to the provinces to secure the second rank of players.

WRC, headed by Australian Ross Turnbull, approached the southern hemisphere's leading players in July, 1995 hoping to sign them for a rugby union circuit run by media millionaire Kerry Packer. The circuit never got off the ground.
"The rugby world found itself under seige from a WRC bent on plunging the game into total disarray by making outrageous payments," Luyt said.
"One wonders if people recognised the magnitude of the task we faced at the time with the prospect of rugby being sold out to a band of poachers.

"We were able to match the amounts of money offered by Ross Turnbull and his gang. In the end we spent almost 60 million rands to stop the WRC but it had to be done to save South African rugby. To save world rugby.
"This was the lead that New Zealand and Australia were waiting for and their players subsequently re-signed for their unions."

SARFU's accounts show that although the union made a trading profit of 18 million rands ($4,000,000) to September 30, 1996, it finished with a loss of 14 million rands ($3,000,000) after the special allocation to the provinces.
